Thanks for the updated order schedule attachment (attached workbook). Our procurement team is reviewing Exhibit A and a few operational questions came up as we map this into our ERP. Quick items below:

1) The schedule shows a "Phase 1" fee floor that kicks in month 1 and then a stepped cap in month 7. When we map billing in our system we need a rule for partial-month transitions — do you invoice actual usage against the serving tier or pro-rate to the new cap?

2) The Sku/line item mapping in tab "SKU_MAP" has three SKU codes (RWI-EMBED-L, RWI-GEN-S, RWI-DED-POOL). We need a canonical description for each SKU for our AP team to reconcile invoices to POs.

3) If CloudEdge triggers a phase change early (e.g., we hit commit earlier than projected), what is the mechanism for applying the new pricing? Is that a billing true-up in the subsequent invoice or immediate re-bill?

We'd like to close this loop before legal signs the final order. Attaching our annotated workbook. Can you confirm the billing behavior and provide suggested invoice line descriptions we can import?

Daniel —

Appreciate the detailed notes and the annotated workbook. High level answers below; I also looped in Karthik (pricing/legal) and Laura (finance/ops) to confirm the canonical SKU language and the billing flow.

1) Partial-month transitions: Our standard approach is to invoice actual usage by SKU for the invoice period. If a phase boundary is crossed mid-invoice period, the new caps/tiers apply for subsequent billing periods and any incremental charge is captured via a true-up line on the next invoice (not a retroactive re-bill). This keeps a single-period invoice consistent and avoids mid-cycle reissues.

2) SKU descriptions: See proposed canonical descriptions in the attached "Redwood_Pricing_ExhibitA_v2.docx". Laura — if those look OK, can finance produce a CSV exportable to CloudEdge's AP template?

3) Early phase change: We treat an early trigger as an accelerated effective date. Operationally we: (a) record the effective date when both parties confirm (email is sufficient), (b) apply new pricing to subsequent invoices and (c) true-up any difference in the first invoice after the change. If CloudEdge prefers immediate re-bill we can discuss but legal usually avoids mid-period re-issuance.

Next steps: Karthik to surface any legal constraints (orderform language) and Laura will provide exportable invoice descriptions. If acceptable, we'll update Exhibit A with a short "billing mechanics" paragraph to append to the schedule.

Best,

Daniel / Vanessa —

Thanks — quick legal note and proposed contract language to keep mechanics explicit in the orderform so there's no downstream ambiguity: see included suggested paragraph (paste below).

Suggested language (for internal comment):
"Billing mechanics and phase transitions: Pricing in Exhibit A will be applied on a per-invoice-period basis. If Customer's usage meets or exceeds a phase threshold mid-invoice-period, the pricing applicable to the higher phase will be effective on the first day of the invoice period following the confirmed phase change. The invoice immediately following a confirmed phase change will include a single true-up line item reflecting the delta between amounts invoiced for the period in which the threshold was met and the amounts that would have been invoiced had the higher phase pricing been effective for that period. Parties may, by mutual written agreement, elect to apply a different effective date or re-issue invoices; absent such agreement, Redwood will not perform mid-period re-bills."

With that language, we address (1) partial month transitions (no mid-period re-bills by default), (2) early triggers (true-up on next invoice) and (3) requirement for mutual written agreement for special handling.

Two operational asks before I sign off: (A) Vanessa/Finance to confirm the canonical SKU descriptions and (B) Procurement to confirm the CloudEdge ERP-friendly PO line mapping (column names) so we can add a one-line import guidance to Exhibit A.
